reasoning_traces.think:
The generalized extinction effect operates as a dual mechanism: it both extinguishes specific conditioned responses and induces broader generalization across related reflexes. This duality arises from Pavlov’s observation that extinction of one conditioned reflex leads to extinction of others sharing a common unconditioned reflex (homogeneous) or differing ones (heterogeneous). Mathematically, this can be modeled as a conditional probability distribution P(E|C) where C represents conditioned stimuli and E denotes extinction outcomes. The homogeneity case implies a shared prior over U, while heterogeneity introduces distinct priors. These primitives form a dual structure in GSI’s Bayesian framework—extinction acts as a posterior update that propagates through stimulus manifolds. In GSE, these dynamics manifest as state transitions governed by feedback loops: when a stimulus is no longer reinforced, the organism shifts to a new internal state reflecting reduced expectation. The failure mode occurs when extinction does not generalize properly due to insufficient reinforcement history or inconsistent environmental cues.
